compiled_state.title: [brainstorm/preplanning]: operational atomicity check — detect artifact-reference desync patterns in AC generation
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Context

DSO planning skills (brainstorm, preplanning, implementation-plan) evaluate features at the capability level but never surface operational-coordination requirements: the pattern where one script writes an artifact X while a separate file Y that references X is left stale in the same change. This produced the release.sh + marketplace.json desync that broke a real plugin release. This epic teaches planning to detect artifact-reference couplings and require atomic co-update, surfaced as an acceptance criterion before implementation, seeded by a registry bootstrapped from the codebase.

Terminology: "AC" = Acceptance Criterion (a human-readable task field). A "writer" is a file in a story's file-impact table with action create or modify whose output is consumed by a registered downstream reference. "touches" = a file appears in the story file-impact table with action create or modify.

## Success Criteria

- SC1: A new Category 8 "Operational Atomicity / Artifact-Reference Desync" is added to the red-team-reviewer story_review taxonomy and the taxonomy_category output enum gains the value operational_atomicity. During story-map review, for a story that touches a registered writer, the reviewer emits a finding whose AC names the paired referencing file and requires atomic same-commit update. Registry-backed findings are authoritative; LLM-inferred findings carry confidence: advisory and are suppressible via SC8. The registry is injected into the reviewer via the orchestrator dispatch arguments at the path in registry.antipattern_path. A Category 8 finding suppresses a parallel Category 6 finding for the same pair; rename/remove cases defer to Category 7.
  Verify-intent: a preplanning run over a fixture story editing a registered writer emits a finding with taxonomy_category=operational_atomicity and an AC string naming the paired referencing file.
- SC2: ast-grep is reclassified from optional to required in the dependency phase of onboarding/SKILL.md and INSTALL.md; onboarding hard-exits non-zero with install remediation when ast-grep is absent, or when the only sg on PATH is the Linux shadow-utils setgid /usr/bin/sg. Detection uses an identity probe (parse sg --version; accept only if it identifies ast-grep at version >= 0.20), never a bare command -v sg. All DSO scripts invoke the long-form ast-grep binary.
  Verify-intent: an onboarding run with ast-grep absent and a decoy setgid sg exits non-zero and the error output contains "ast-grep" plus a recommended install command.
- SC3: A new bootstrap migration script fans out sub-agents over chunked codebase slices, each running ast-grep to emit (file, normalized_path, role, line, snippet) tuples (map), joined by an equijoin on the realpath-normalized path (reduce). A pair is admitted only when all hold: exact realpath-normalized path, a recognized write idiom (shell > / >>, tee, sed -i, jq write-to-file, Python open(w)/Path.write_text, Node fs.writeFileSync, Ruby File.open(w)/File.write, Go os.WriteFile; vocabulary externally extensible via registry config), and writer and reference in different files. Ambiguous/inferred pairs are out of scope for the migration.
  Verify-intent: bootstrap over a fixture repo emits output equal to a sorted newline-delimited "writer_realpath<TAB>reference_realpath" manifest exactly (no missing/extra); near-miss fixtures (same-file self-reference; cross-file read-only) are absent.
- SC4: implementation-plan/SKILL.md emits, for any task that adds, modifies, or removes a dso-config.conf key, a separate child sub-task (testing_mode GREEN) titled "Document <key> in CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md" carrying a depends_on link to the parent task. This child sub-task supersedes the generic doc-router path for config keys (no duplicate documentation task).
  Verify-intent: an implementation-plan run on a key-adding task yields that child sub-task whose depends_on points to the parent task id.
- SC5: The Category 8 consumption point reads the antipattern registry at registry.antipattern_path. Registry schema (this epic codes against this shape; clear-fairy may ship it, else a local fixture supplies it): a YAML file whose records are {file_class: glob, pattern: regex or ast-grep query, audit_task_template: string} plus a top-level schema_version. When present, a matching file_class injects a pre-emptive audit task from audit_task_template. When absent, clean no-op logging "registry absent"; when present-but-unparseable, clean no-op logging "registry unreadable" (distinct). Adaptation to clear-fairy's final schema is limited to updating registry.antipattern_path + schema_version; no migration code is owned here.
  Verify-intent: registry absent -> completes, logs "registry absent"; corrupt fixture -> completes, logs "registry unreadable"; valid fixture -> injects the audit task.
- SC6: When a registered referencing file is not co-updatable in the same commit, classified by the union (git check-ignore | generated-path heuristic reusing is_generated_file() patterns | cross-repo URL in the reference | branch-protected via gh api, where a 404 is treated as not-protected and the branch-protection result is cached per-branch), the gate emits a deferred-coordination note recorded as a story consideration that preplanning/sprint consume by creating a follow-up coordination task, instead of an unachievable atomic-update AC. The note format contract is named in the preplanning/sprint acceptance criteria so the receiving behavior is testable.
  Verify-intent: a generated-file fixture yields a deferred-coordination consideration and a follow-up task, not a hard atomic-update AC.
- SC7: A re-runnable registry-refresh command (sharing a normalize-and-sort library with the bootstrap; idempotent sort-dedup on write) detects writer/reference pairs added since the last run.
  Verify-intent: a re-run on a fixture repo with one newly-added pair surfaces exactly that pair as an update candidate; a no-change re-run surfaces nothing.
- SC8: A config key review.atomicity_inference_enabled (default false; documented in CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md) gates only the Category 8 LLM-inference pass; the deterministic registry pass always runs. The SC4 story is sequenced before the SC8 story so SC8's key documentation follows the G11-M2 pattern.
  Verify-intent: with the key false, a planning run emits zero confidence: advisory findings but still emits registry-backed findings.

## Closure Checks

- The plugin-shipped seed registry contains the pairs release.sh<->marketplace.json, *.conf<->CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md, and plugin.json<->marketplace source ref.
- onboarding docs list ast-grep as required (minimum version >= 0.20) with install instructions (cargo/npm/brew) and document the /usr/bin/sg shadow-utils collision.
- red-team-reviewer.md taxonomy_category enum includes the value operational_atomicity.
- review.atomicity_inference_enabled and registry.antipattern_path are documented in CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md.
- The shared normalize-and-sort registry library file exists and is sourced by both the bootstrap and refresh scripts.

## Dependencies

- clear-fairy / 7575-5a90 (depends_on) for the antipattern registry artifact consumed by SC5 only. All other SCs have no external dependency. The 85cb idempotent-task-semantics relationship was reviewed and overridden (our state-check ACs hold regardless of how idempotency is later formalized).

## Approach

Hybrid detection: a plugin-shipped seed registry of artifact-reference pairs (YAML) plus a project-local overlay, read deterministically by a new Category 8 pass in the red-team-reviewer at preplanning time, supplemented by an LLM inference pass for novel couplings (advisory, suppressible). Bootstrap migration uses ast-grep as a one-engine polyglot extractor (per-file tuple emit) plus an external equijoin on the realpath-normalized path (ast-grep matches within a file only). ast-grep is upgraded to a required onboarding dependency with shadow-utils /usr/bin/sg disambiguation. This converged with prior art: deterministic registry/declaration over inference for anything that gates (changesets fixed/linked, release-please extra-files, syncpack), one tree-sitter engine over per-language plugins, and inference confined to advisory triage. clear-fairy delivers the antipattern registry (G6-M2); this epic owns its consumption (G6-M3), the config-key/doc pairing (G11-M2), and the core atomicity check.

## Scenario Analysis

- setgid /usr/bin/sg shadows ast-grep so a bare guard runs the wrong binary (critical) - mitigated by SC2 identity probe + invoking ast-grep.
- Equijoin path normalization across sub-agents produces false/missed pairs (high) - mitigated by SC3 realpath normalization.
- Category 8 LLM-inference fires non-deterministically across runs (high) - mitigated by deterministic registry authority + SC8 toggle + advisory confidence.
- Bootstrap sub-agents truncate tuple lists at context limit with no error (high) - operational risk for preplanning.
- G6-M3 no-op when registry absent is indistinguishable from unreadable (medium) - mitigated by SC5 distinct diagnostics.
- Seed + overlay have no merge protocol; stale overlay shadows updated seed (high) - registry-lifecycle risk for preplanning.
- Onboarding block does not propagate to CI; CI silently skips the gate (high) - mitigated by a CI ast-grep precondition before planning jobs.
- Bootstrap is one-time; registry goes stale (high) - mitigated by SC7 refresh.
- Write-idiom set not configurable; project idioms produce no pairs (high) - mitigated by SC3 extensible vocabulary.
- No knob to disable Category 8 inference (medium) - mitigated by SC8.
- Equijoin assumes path stability; symlinks/aliases produce phantom/missed pairs (high) - mitigated by SC3 realpath resolution.
- Atomic-co-update AC is unachievable for generated/cross-repo/branch-protected files (high) - mitigated by SC6 deferred-coordination note.
- Preplanning gate assumes stories name artifacts; high-abstraction stories miss the registry (high) - partially mitigated by Category 8 inference pass.
- G6-M3 depends_on clear-fairy assumes ordered execution; parallel dispatch can race / read a partial registry (medium) - mitigated by SC5 degradation.

## Cross-Epic Interactions

- CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md (with many config-adding epics, e.g. 88d2-6756, dso-0wi2, 230a-344a, 371f-cfc3, 7952-9785): SC4 edits implementation-plan/SKILL.md only; CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md itself is edited at story-run time, so merge risk is at story-run time, not epic-merge time. Coordinate key namespacing.
- Onboarding ast-grep enforcement (with 70d5 Java stack, d97a /dso:doctor, ed62 cross-runner, c206 Strata SDK, w21-bsnz): single ast-grep required-dependency check with setgid disambiguation; /dso:doctor is a future consumer of the same check, not modified here; coordinate hard-exit semantics with Java onboarding sharing onboarding/SKILL.md.
- red-team-reviewer Category 8 / planning AC injection (with 857d-a35a security declarations, 853a-c719 observability, 94ed-f55c intent allocation, af26-dd5a impl-plan enforcement): Category 8 coexists as an independent taxonomy layer.
- red-team-reviewer agent extraction (dso-8l5h): sequence agent extraction before Category 8 edits to avoid dispatch-site churn.
- Antipattern-registry schema (99f1-153c fix-bug recurrence scan, clear-fairy/7575-5a90): SC5 consumes a read-only registry; no schema ownership here.

## Prompt Alignment Findings

- Matched signal: agent definitions / skill-file modifications (red-team-reviewer.md, onboarding, implementation-plan).
- Behavioral review (bot-psychologist): define the registry path/schema and absent-behavior (addressed by SC5); add operational_atomicity to the taxonomy_category enum (Closure Check); gate the LLM-inference half behind a structural test and mark it confidence: advisory (SC1/SC8); add explicit dedup rules so Category 8 does not double-emit against Category 6 (Consumer Impact) or Category 7 (Residual References); define writer/touches (glossary); for onboarding use the version-line identity probe, not bare command -v sg (SC2). G11-M2 should cover add/modify/remove and emit a separate child sub-task, not an AC bullet (SC4).
- Recommendations carried into implementation-plan: define the full Category 8 finding schema (taxonomy_category, AC string, confidence) once and reference it from SC1 and SC8.

### Planning Intelligence Log

- Gap analysis (Step 1): all user-named artifacts covered; Parts executed: Part A artifact check, Part B technical self-review, Part C shared artifact impact (behavioral-prohibition mode; 3 descoped consumers flagged).
- Web research (Step 2.6): triggered. Bright-line conditions that fired: Unfamiliar dependency (ast-grep required), Migration (bootstrap migration), Novel architectural pattern (map/reduce cross-file join). Prior-art convergence synthesis recorded.
- Scenario analysis (Step 2.75): triggered. Scenarios surviving blue team filter: 14.
- Practitioner-requested additional cycles: none via gate; fidelity ran 3 revision cycles (structural re-review after SC count 5->8).
- Follow-on scrutiny (Step 0): not triggered.
- Feasibility resolution (Step 2.5): triggered - feasibility reviewer ran (integration signals: ast-grep); no FEASIBILITY_GAP (no score < 3).
- LLM-instruction signal (Step 5): triggered - keyword: agent definitions; bot-psychologist dispatched.
- Scale context (Step 0): not applicable (no volume decision; planning-time static check).

comments.body:
Scope expansion (2026-04-26, from docs/proposed-mitigations-4-26.md):

Two mitigations absorbed into this epic's atomicity-check scope:

- **G6-M3** — Generalize the operational-atomicity check to also cover known-antipattern audits at brainstorm/preplanning time. When an epic touches a file class associated with a known antipattern (shell hooks → CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT, runners → semantic drift, etc.), inject a pre-emptive task: 'Audit for <antipattern> across all files in scope before implementation begins.' The known-antipattern registry is delivered by New Epic A (static-analysis defense layer) per docs/new-epics-4-26.md; this epic consumes the registry at planning time.
- **G11-M2** — Implementation-plan templated paired sub-task: when a task adds a config key in dso-config.conf or any *.conf, mandatorily emit a paired sub-task documenting the key in CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md (description, type, default, scope, example). Same atomicity pattern as the artifact-desync case (release.sh + marketplace.json that motivated this epic): two artifacts must update together.

Rationale: this epic's existing scope is the artifact-reference desync pattern (Script A creates artifact X, file Y references X but is not updated atomically). Both additions extend the same mechanism to additional artifact pairs (code + antipattern audit; config-key + reference doc). The detection-injection point (red-team-reviewer or AC generation) is the same.

This epic has no children yet (scrutiny:pending); decomposition will pick up the new SCs naturally. Note: tag scrutiny:pending should be cleared once brainstorm runs on this epic.
